mutants.label: load_gaps-reverts-to-inferred-frame
frame_for-strict-disabled
mutants.why: records is always a list of per-row dicts (orient="row"), and for that input shape polars 1.44.2's DataFrame constructor ignores the `strict` flag entirely -- it goes through an append-based row builder, not the cast path `strict` documents ("cast to that data type or, if casting is not possible, set to null"). Verified empirically with strict=True vs strict=False side by side across 10 dtype/value combinations spanning every dtype _DUCKDB_TO_POLARS_DTYPE can produce: a bare string into Float64/Int64/Boolean/Datetime columns, an out-of-range int into Int32, a fractional float into Int32, a python int into a String column, a list into Float64, and an epoch int into Date -- every pair raised (or silently truncated) identically regardless of strict. `pl.DataFrame(records, schema=schema, strict=False)` therefore behaves byte-for-byte like the unmutated `pl.DataFrame(records, schema=schema)` for every record this warehouse ever builds, so test_frame_for_rejects_value_of_wrong_type cannot distinguish the two: the raise it asserts on comes from the row-builder rejecting an unappendable value, a behavior `strict` does not gate on this call shape. (Column-oriented input -- pl.DataFrame({"x": ["sixty"]}, schema=..., strict=False) -- does silently null instead of raising, confirming strict is live in general; it just never reaches that code path here.)

mutants.label: schema-lookup-ignores-table_schema
mutants.why: Every table _frame_for is ever called against lives in the `raw` schema (raw.asos_hourly, raw.resolved_windows, raw.ingest_gaps, and the scratch table the unmapped-type test creates are all `create table raw.x`), and the test database has no second schema defining a same-named table -- DuckDB's own `information_schema`/`pg_catalog`/`main` schemas don't declare tables named asos_hourly, resolved_windows, ingest_gaps, or scratch_x. Dropping the `table_schema = ?` predicate therefore returns the identical single-row-per-column result set in every test this suite runs. Verified empirically: the full suite stays green under this mutation.
mutants.find:
"select column_name, data_type from information_schema.columns "
            "where table_schema = ? and table_name = ?",
            [table_schema, table_name],
